questions.question: What is the difference between large stock, small stock and poultry? Give an example of each.
questions.expected_answer: Large stock are big farm animals, mainly cattle. Small stock are smaller farm animals, such as sheep, goats and pigs. Poultry are farm birds, such as chickens, ducks, geese, turkeys and ostriches.

questions.question: Name three products we get from cattle and two from sheep.
questions.expected_answer: From cattle: beef, milk, leather and dung. From sheep: mutton or lamb, and wool.

questions.question: Name three ways farmers look after their animals, and explain what overgrazing is.
questions.expected_answer: Farmers give their animals food, clean water and shelter; they dip or spray them against ticks, vaccinate them and call a vet when they are sick; they keep them safe in kraals and behind fences. Overgrazing is when too many animals eat all the grass, so the soil is left bare and washes away.
